draft.title: Properties of quadrilaterals
card: A parallelogram has \(AB \parallel DC\) and \(AD \parallel BC\). In parallelogram ABCD, diagonal AC splits it into triangles ABC and CDA.

In triangles ABC and CDA: \(\angle BAC = \angle DCA\) (alternate angles, \(AB \parallel DC\)). \(\angle BCA = \angle DAC\) (alternate angles, \(AD \parallel BC\)). AC is a common side. So the triangles are congruent (AAS).
Matching sides of congruent triangles are equal. So \(AB = CD\) and \(AD = BC\) (matching sides of congruent triangles). Opposite sides are equal.

The diagonals meet at M. In triangles AMB and CMD, alternate angles are equal (\(AB \parallel DC\)), and \(AB = CD\) from above. The triangles are congruent (AAS), so \(AM = CM\) and \(BM = DM\): the diagonals bisect each other.
draft.remember: Congruent triangles inside a parallelogram explain why its opposite sides are equal and its diagonals bisect each other.

a.q: In the proof that \(\angle BAC = \angle DCA\) in parallelogram ABCD, which reason is given?
opts: Angles in a triangle add to \(180^{\circ}\)
a.why: AC cuts the parallel lines AB and DC, so the angles on opposite sides of AC are alternate angles and are equal. Co-interior angles would add to \(180^{\circ}\), not be equal.
a.clue: AC crosses two parallel lines. Which angle pair is it?

b.q: Triangles ABC and CDA in a parallelogram have two pairs of equal angles and share side AC. Which test shows they are congruent?
b.why: There are two pairs of equal angles and one common side, so the test is AAS. SSS and SAS need sides given. RHS needs a right angle.
b.clue: Count the equal angles and the equal side.

problems.detail: The diagonals step says only 'alternate angles are equal' without naming the pairs (\(\angle MAB = \angle MCD\), \(\angle MBA = \angle MDC\)). A point that teaches giving a reason for each matching angle should name both pairs, or students may not see which angles are meant.

proposal.title: Proving properties of quadrilaterals
card: A parallelogram has both pairs of opposite sides parallel. In parallelogram ABCD, AB is parallel to DC and AD is parallel to BC. Diagonal AC splits it into triangles ABC and CDA.

In triangles ABC and CDA: angle BAC equals angle DCA (alternate angles, AB parallel to DC). Angle BCA equals angle DAC (alternate angles, AD parallel to BC). AC is a common side. So the triangles are congruent (AAS).
Matching sides of congruent triangles are equal. So \(AB = CD\) and \(AD = BC\) (matching sides of congruent triangles). The opposite sides of a parallelogram are equal.

The diagonals meet at M. In triangles AMB and CMD: angle MAB equals angle MCD and angle MBA equals angle MDC (both alternate angles, AB parallel to DC), and \(AB = CD\) (proved above). So the triangles are congruent (AAS), giving \(AM = CM\) and \(BM = DM\): the diagonals bisect each other.
proposal.remember: Congruent triangles inside a parallelogram explain why its opposite sides are equal and its diagonals bisect each other.

a.q: In the proof that angle BAC equals angle DCA in parallelogram ABCD, which reason is given?
opts: Alternate angles, AB parallel to DC
Co-interior angles, AB parallel to DC
Vertically opposite angles at A and C
Angles in a triangle add to \(180^{\circ}\)
a.why: AC cuts the parallel lines AB and DC, and the two angles sit on opposite sides of AC, so they are alternate angles and are equal. Co-interior angles add to \(180^{\circ}\), so they would not give equal angles.
a.clue: AC crosses two parallel lines. Which angle pair is equal?

b.q: Triangles ABC and CDA in a parallelogram have two pairs of equal angles and share side AC. Which test shows they are congruent?
b.why: There are two pairs of equal angles and one equal side, so the test is AAS. SSS needs three pairs of sides and SAS needs two pairs of sides. RHS needs a right angle.
b.clue: Count the equal angles and the equal sides.

wants.why: Seeing the vertices, the parallel sides and the diagonals lets students follow which triangles and angles each step of the proof names.
